notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.5.4.3 SR1: "The BLANK WHEN ZERO clause can be specified only for an elementary item whose PICTURE is specified as numeric or numeric edited". The restriction is implemented at 85: CheckElementaryOnlyClauses refuses the clause on a group entry (COBOL2403) and CheckClauseSubjectsPass.Run refuses it, through BlankWhenZeroViolation, on an elementary item whose category is not numeric or numeric edited (COBOL2405); the level 66 and 88 formats take no such clause. Not implemented for 85: the numeric PICTURE that carries the symbol S. PictureComposition.Validate applies the 2023 rule (§2023:13.18.40.3 SR22, "Neither the symbol 'S' nor the symbol '*' shall be specified") with no edition test, so PIC S9(4) BLANK WHEN ZERO draws COBOL1934 at 85. The 1985 text bars the asterisk only (§1985:VI.5.9.3 SR7) and has no rule on S; a PICTURE of S and 9 is numeric, and §1985:VI.5.4.4 GR2 says what the clause does to it. The refusal is the 2002 change §2002:F.1 item 33: "The previous COBOL standard did not specify whether BLANK WHEN ZERO for a numeric item with a picture character-string including an 'S' was syntactically valid" and "The implementor will now provide a syntax error for such an occurrence". Probed at --std 85: accepted and blanked at zero are PIC 9(4), ZZZ9, 9(3)V99, -9(3).99, $$$9.99CR and 99PP; refused are PIC X(3), A(3), XBX, X(2)/X, 9X, A9, a group entry and a USAGE INDEX item; refused and legal are PIC S9(4) and PIC S9(3) SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE. The witness is PIC X(3) BLANK WHEN ZERO, refused with COBOL2405.

next.reason: 1985 admits BLANK WHEN ZERO for any elementary item 'whose PICTURE is specified as numeric or numeric edited'; no 1985 rule bars the symbol S. §2023:13.18.8.3 SR1 narrows this to 'category numeric-edited or ... numeric without the picture symbol S', so PIC S9(4) BLANK WHEN ZERO, legal in 1985, is refused. §2023:13.16.3 SR11 keeps the elementary-only part. The usage requirement (§2023:13.18.8.3 SR2) answers 1985 SR2, not this rule. Both are compile-time rules.
